Dedup-ON golden etalon. Re-captured at atlas format v7, again once the QUAD_*
hint started firing, and (for the D4 etalon) once alias rings became canonically
rotated; the region dumps are unaffected by all three.
Captured on the tree that shipped post-trim + D4-canonical dedup, AFTER
byte-equal vertex-block sharing landed (blocks fold across pages, so an etalon
captured before it would not match) and AFTER block identity gained the
trim_offset terms. Every frame here sits on its own canvas at its own offset, so
none of the 6 folds shares a block — the region dump is unchanged by that rule,
only the vertex blob length is, which is why the dump and the SHA move apart.
Single-threaded (nt_builder_set_threads(ctx, 1), NT_BUILDER_THREADS=1),
nt_atlas_opts_defaults() unmodified — dedup ON, allowed_transforms = ALL.
Fixture: tests/unit/test_helpers/atlas_dedup_fixture.h, all 10 frames via
atlas_dedup_fixture_add (4 art states on 10 distinct canvas sizes/offsets, so
folding is reachable only after the alpha trim). 10 frames -> 4 placements.
Atlas name "dedup_golden" — the name seeds the texture page resource ids, so
the SHA depends on it; re-capture with any other name will not match.
etalon_dedup_on sha256 4ace0c4e69e9e75b59360959e6cd7b04a1b681506dfd4cbbaa035989d9588e5e
test_atlas_transform_mask::test_golden_byte_identity_dedup_on re-packs the same
fixture, asserts the pack still folds to 4 distinct placements, then asserts
byte-identity against this dump + sha256 pair.

Dedup-D4 golden etalon.
Same tree and same single-threaded capture. Every fold in etalon_dedup_on is at
relative transform identity, so it never reaches derived alias geometry,
re-triangulation or the composed-transform UV bake — this second etalon is the
byte fence over exactly those.
Fixture: tests/unit/test_helpers/atlas_dedup_f_fixture.h via
atlas_dedup_f_fixture_add_concave — all eight orientations of the 9x13 'F' at
the atlas-default concave shape, allowed_transforms = ALL, dedup inherited.
8 frames -> 1 placement, 0 exact folds, 7 D4 folds.
The packer places the single rectangle at identity, so each region's transform
IS its relative transform, and the dump reads back the inverse permutation
0 1 2 3 4 6 5 7 — the ROT90/ROT270 swap is what makes this etalon sensitive to
a relabelling of the D4 element codes.
Atlas name "dedup_d4_golden" — same name-seeds-the-SHA caveat.
etalon_dedup_d4 sha256 e257e751ef98f46bf44ba72c1f47a1c0a11b87a749a27c6ebb6f7029f5ff0c01
test_atlas_transform_mask::test_golden_byte_identity_dedup_d4 re-packs the
fixture, asserts one placement and eight pairwise-distinct region transforms,
then asserts byte-identity against this dump + sha256 pair.

To regenerate either etalon after an INTENTIONAL dedup or packer change: run
test_atlas_transform_mask, then take the SHA-256 of
build/tests/tmp/<name>.ntpack and copy build/tests/tmp/<name>_dump.txt over the
dump file (the test also prints the current dump on divergence), where <name> is
dedup_golden or dedup_d4_golden. Keep every file LF — pinned in .gitattributes.
